memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"After the LORD brings you into the land of the Canaanites and gives it to you,
as he promised on oath to you and your ancestors, you are to give over to the
LORD the first offspring of every womb. All the firstborn males of your
livestock belong to the LORD." - Ex 13:11-12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God returns to the firstborn, and He ties it to the land He is giving them.

There is an order here worth noticing. First God gives; then Israel gives back.
The land was His gift before any of it was theirs to offer. They would give from
what He had already provided.

That order never changes. David understood it centuries later when the people
gave generously for the temple: "Everything comes from you, and we have given
you only what comes from your hand" (1 Chr 29:14). We never give God anything He
did not first give us.

This protects us from two errors. It guards against pride, because there is
nothing in our hands to boast about. And it guards against fear, because giving
does not diminish us when the Giver is our supply.

Notice the phrase "as he promised on oath." Israel's giving rested on God's
faithfulness, not the other way round. They did not give in order to make God
generous. They gave because He already had been.

The same is true of us. We do not give to secure God's blessing. That would turn
worship into a transaction. We give because in Christ we have already received
more than we can measure (2 Cor 8:9).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you think of your giving as a transaction with God or a response to Him?
2. What has God given you that you have started thinking of as simply yours?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, everything I have came from Your hand. Free me from holding it tightly
and let me give with an open heart. Amen.
